goodsIndustries.name: Agriculture, Forestry, Fishing & Hunting
goodsIndustries.analysis:
Agriculture, forestry, fishing and hunting GDP eased 1.1% month-over-month against a +2.1% year-over-year reading for the March reference month — the monthly softening1 sits against a backdrop of firmer farm-gate prices, with the Saskatchewan canola farm price at CAD$672.81/t in April, up 6.2% year-over-year and 1.8% month-over-month2. Potash proxy Nutrien closed the week at $92.23, up 12.0% year-over-year but down 1.9% week-over-week, easing one input-cost line for Prairie producers while keeping the annual comparison elevated3.

The Agriculture and Forestry pipeline tracks 733 active projects at $8.2B in priced value, split $3.5B agriculture and $4.7B forestry — the Canada Food Security Strategy4, a $3.2B Ontario-led federal program, was added at Proposed status on 2026-06-11, while Drake Meat Processors entered Under Construction in Saskatoon and Atlas Engineered Products Advanced Wood Manufacturing Facility in Clinton, Ontario, reached Approved status this week5.

If canola holds above CAD$670/t and the potash month-over-month softening continues, Prairie farm-gate margins would see input relief into Q3 — only 2 of 464 priced Agriculture rows carry stated values, so the directional read is from commodities and named additions rather than aggregate dollars6. Procurement.json has been empty for eight consecutive weeks, removing visibility into federal agri-program contract awards7.

goodsIndustries.name: Mining, Quarrying & Oil/Gas Extraction
goodsIndustries.analysis:
Mining, quarrying and oil and gas extraction GDP contracted 2.1% month-over-month and 1.5% year-over-year in the March reference month, the largest month-over-month decline in the goods table — the StatCan reading1 diverges sharply from spot and equity benchmarks for the sector's outputs, with the nickel proxy at 45.41, up 111.6% year-over-year and 12.2% week-over-week, iron ore (Vale) at 16.15, up 79.1% year-over-year, and uranium spot at 27.07, up 16.1% year-over-year2. Cameco closed at $149.80, up 59.4% year-over-year, consistent with a supply-side response in uranium markets3.

The Mining and oil/gas pipeline tracks 778 projects at $248.3B in priced value, split $184.8B mining and $63.5B oil and gas, with 8 mining files now Under Review in the federal Impact Assessment Registry — new this week: Eranova Metals BC Molybdenum, FireFly Metals Green Bay Copper in Newfoundland and Labrador, and Marinvest Energy Baie-Comeau LNG Export in Quebec4. Glencore Horne Smelter Emissions Reduction was filed at $300M proposed in Quebec, sitting at the NAICS 21/31-33 boundary5.

The divergence between -2.1% month-over-month output and +111.6% year-over-year nickel suggests volume declines and IAAC review pauses are outweighing price-driven revenue gains in the StatCan series — if nickel and iron ore hold near current levels, breakeven economics for the 651 mining-tagged projects shift, and the Eranova, FireFly, and Glencore Horne files would advance through IAAC and provincial environmental assessment more readily6. The empty procurement.json file removes visibility into federal critical-minerals contract awards7.

goodsIndustries.name: Utilities
goodsIndustries.analysis:
Utilities GDP printed flat month-over-month and -1.6% year-over-year for the March reference month, while the TSX Infrastructure basket closed at 57.56, up 33.0% year-over-year and 2.9% month-over-month — the StatCan output reading1 runs counter to equity-market signals for the sector2. Uranium spot at 27.07 (+16.1% year-over-year) is the relevant feedstock benchmark for the small modular reactor supply chain that links NAICS 22 generation projects to NAICS 21 mining inputs3.

Power and energy is the single largest tracked sector by value at 936 active projects and $614.3B in priced pipeline — new this week: Red Lake Transmission Line in Ontario (Proposed); Des Neiges Wind Farm Secteur Sud and Charlevoix phases at $3.0B (Quebec, Under Construction); Sydney 300MW Hybrid Wind+BESS (Nova Scotia, Proposed); Brighton Mountain Wind (New Brunswick); and Manitoba Large-Scale Hydroelectric Dam4. Bill S-4 (45-1), An Act to amend the Energy Efficiency Act, received first reading on 2026-06-05, with equipment-standard implications across NAICS 22, 23, and 31-335.

The 33.0% year-over-year gain in the TSX Infrastructure basket alongside the -1.6% year-over-year GDP print indicates equity allocation has run ahead of measured output across the 936 utilities projects — if Bill S-4 advances past first reading, equipment-standard tightening would pull-forward retrofit demand. If Sydney NS BESS and Red Lake Transmission move from Proposed to Approved, NAICS 22 capex velocity would accelerate, and uranium price strength supports the Saskatchewan uranium-feedstock investment thesis6.

goodsIndustries.name: Construction
goodsIndustries.analysis:
Construction GDP fell 0.6% month-over-month and 1.5% year-over-year for the March reference month, while three of the sector's primary input commodities rose week-over-week — the SLX steel ETF closed at $111.39, up 73.4% year-over-year and 4.7% week-over-week1; iron ore (Vale) at 16.15, up 79.1% year-over-year and 7.7% week-over-week2; lumber futures at $630.50, up 7.9% month-over-month and 3.0% week-over-week3. The combined steel and iron-ore moves directly compress fixed-price contractor margins on infrastructure bids.

The construction pipeline (infrastructure + residential + commercial_mixed) is the broadest by count at 2,005 active projects with $288.7B in priced value, split $223.9B infrastructure, $36.2B residential, and $28.6B commercial mixed-use — new this week: Alberton Wastewater and Stormwater (Prince Edward Island, Approved); Rideau Canal Wall Repairs (Ontario, Under Review); and Parks Canada Brazeau Lake Bridge Replacement (Alberta, Under Review), with 18 infrastructure rows added in total4. Bill S-4 (45-1) building-code amendments received first reading on 2026-06-05 with implications for new construction equipment standards5.

Job Bank Atom feed postings for 2026-06-15 were concentrated in construction trades — concrete, framing, electrical, roofing, masonry — across Toronto, Vancouver, Calgary, Edmonton, Winnipeg, Regina, and Saint John, indicating labour demand has not retraced with the GDP reading — if steel and iron ore hold above current levels, fixed-price infrastructure bids would re-price upward on the next tender cycle, and if lumber stabilizes month-over-month, residential builders would see input-cost relief on the 271 residential-tagged projects6.

goodsIndustries.name: Manufacturing
goodsIndustries.analysis:
Manufacturing GDP rose 0.4% month-over-month while remaining down 2.5% year-over-year, the largest year-over-year decline in the goods table — the month-over-month stabilization1 coincides with sharp moves in the sector's primary input commodities: steel SLX at $111.39, up 73.4% year-over-year2; iron ore at 16.15, up 79.1% year-over-year3; nickel proxy at 45.41, up 111.6% year-over-year, feeding directly into EV battery cathode economics for the Ontario and Quebec EV supply chain4.

The manufacturing pipeline tracks 362 active projects at $85.4B in priced value, with 6 rows added this week — CGC Inc. Wheatland County Wallboard Manufacturing Plant ($210M, Alberta) reached Complete status, and Glencore Horne Smelter Emissions Reduction was filed at $300M proposed in Quebec, the largest new-this-week capex point5. Manufacturing job postings concentrated in Toronto (Del Industrial Metals, Powerline Plus, Qualified Metal Fabricators, Fiera Foods), Halifax (IMP Aerospace and Defence), and Montreal6.

The +0.4% month-over-month against -2.5% year-over-year suggests partial stabilization within a still-contracting annual trajectory — if the month-over-month direction carries forward and steel and iron-ore prices retrace, the year-over-year gap would narrow into Q3. If nickel strength persists, EV-battery-aligned manufacturing files in Ontario and Quebec gain capex pull, and Bill S-4 (45-1) equipment-standard amendments would land on industrial-process retrofits across the 362 tracked projects7.
